sanskrit: santi nānāvidhā lokā yāṃs tvaṃ śakra na paśyasi paśyāmi yān ahaṃ lokān ekapatnyaś ca yāḥ striyaḥ
english: There exist worlds of many kinds, O Śakra, which you do not behold — worlds that I behold, and likewise the women who are faithful to a single husband.

sanskrit: karmabhiś cāpi suśubhaiḥ suvratā ṛṣayas tathā saśarīrā hi tān yānti brāhmaṇāḥ śubhavṛttayaḥ
english: By their wholly auspicious deeds the seers of firm vows, and the Brāhmaṇas of pure conduct, attain those worlds in their very bodies.

sanskrit: śarīranyāsamokṣeṇa manasā nirmalena ca svapnabhūtāṃś ca tāṃl lokān paśyantīhāpi suvratāḥ
english: And those of firm vows, by laying down the body in release and through a mind made spotless, behold even here those worlds that are like a dream.

sanskrit: te tu lokāḥ sahasrākṣa śṛṇu yādṛgguṇānvitāḥ na tatra kramate kālo na jarā na ca pāpakam tathānyan nāśubhaṃ kiṃ cin na vyādhis tatra na klamaḥ
english: And those worlds, O thousand-eyed one — hear with what qualities they are endowed. There time does not advance, nor old age, nor any evil; nor anything else inauspicious, no disease there, and no fatigue.

sanskrit: yad yac ca gāvo manasā tasmin vāñchanti vāsava tat sarvaṃ prāpayanti sma mama pratyakṣadarśanāt kāmagāḥ kāmacāriṇyaḥ kāmāt kāmāṃś ca bhuñjate
english: And whatever the cattle there desire in their minds, O Vāsava, all that they obtain by beholding me directly; going where they wish, roaming where they please, at will they enjoy their every wish.

sanskrit: vāpyaḥ sarāṃsi sarito vividhāni vanāni ca gṛhāṇi parvatāś caiva yāvad dravyaṃ ca kiṃ cana
english: Tanks, lakes, rivers, and forests of many kinds, dwellings and mountains too, and whatever substance there may be —

sanskrit: manojñaṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ sarvaṃ tatra pradṛśyate īdṛśān viddhi tāṃl lokān nāsti lokas tato 'dhikaḥ
english: all that is pleasing to every being is seen there. Know those worlds to be of such a kind; there is no world higher than that.

sanskrit: tatra sarvasahāḥ kṣāntā vatsalā guruvartinaḥ ahaṃkārair virahitā yānti śakra narottamāḥ
english: To that place go, O Śakra, the best of men — all-enduring, patient, affectionate, devoted to their elders, and wholly free of egotism.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvamāṃsāni na bhakṣayīta; pumān sadā yāvad antāya yuktaḥ mātāpitror arcitā satyayuktaḥ; śuśrūṣitā brāhmaṇānām anindyaḥ
english: The man who never eats flesh of any kind, ever devoted until his end, who honors his mother and father, joined to truth, a server of the Brāhmaṇas, blameless —

sanskrit: akrodhano goṣu tathā dvijeṣu; dharme rato guruśuśrūṣakaś ca yāvajjīvaṃ satyavṛtte rataś ca; dāne rato yaḥ kṣamī cāparādhe
english: free of anger toward cattle and toward the twice-born, delighting in dharma, a servant of his elders, devoted lifelong to the practice of truth, given to charity, and forgiving of offense —

sanskrit: mṛdur dānto devaparāyaṇaś ca; sarvātithiś cāpi tathā dayāvān īdṛgguṇo mānavaḥ saṃprayāti; lokaṃ gavāṃ śāśvataṃ cāvyayaṃ ca
english: gentle, self-controlled, devoted to the gods, hospitable to all guests and full of compassion — a man endowed with such qualities proceeds to the world of cattle, eternal and imperishable.

sanskrit: na pāradārī paśyati lokam enaṃ; na vai gurughno na mṛṣāpralāpī sadāpavādī brāhmaṇaḥ śāntavedo; doṣair anyair yaś ca yukto durātmā
english: No adulterer beholds this world, nor the slayer of a teacher, nor the babbler of falsehood, nor the forever-slandering Brāhmaṇa who has let his Vedic learning lapse, nor the evil-souled one yoked to other faults.

sanskrit: na mitradhruṅ naikṛtikaḥ kṛtaghnaḥ; śaṭho 'nṛjur dharmavidveṣakaś ca na brahmahā manasāpi prapaśyed; gavāṃ lokaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ nivāsam
english: No betrayer of a friend, no deceiver, no ingrate, no rogue, no crooked man, no hater of dharma, no slayer of a Brāhmaṇa may even in his mind behold the world of cattle, the dwelling of those who have done meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ naipuṇena sureśvara gopradānaratānāṃ tu phalaṃ śṛṇu śatakrato
english: All this has been told you with precision, O lord of the gods; now hear the fruit that belongs to those devoted to the gift of cattle, O performer of a hundred rites.

sanskrit: dāyādyalabdhair arthair yo gāḥ krītvā saṃprayacchati dharmārjitadhanakrītān sa lokān aśnute 'kṣayān
english: He who, having bought cattle with wealth obtained as his rightful inheritance, gives them away, attains imperishable worlds purchased with righteously gained riches.

sanskrit: yo vai dyūte dhanaṃ jitvā gāḥ krītvā saṃprayacchati sa divyam ayutaṃ śakra varṣāṇāṃ phalam aśnute
english: He who, having won wealth at dice, buys cattle and gives them away, enjoys, O Śakra, a divine reward lasting ten thousand years.

sanskrit: dāyādyā yasya vai gāvo nyāyapūrvair upārjitāḥ pradattās tāḥ pradātṝṇāṃ saṃbhavanty akṣayā dhruvāḥ
english: Cattle that are a man's inheritance, gained by lawful means and then bestowed, become for their givers imperishable and enduring.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca yo dadyād gāḥ suśuddhena cetasā tasyāpīhākṣayāṃl lokān dhruvān viddhi śacīpate
english: And he who, having received cattle, gives them away with a wholly purified heart — know, O husband of Śacī, that for him too the worlds here are imperishable and enduring.

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti satyaṃ ca yo brūyān niyatendriyaḥ gurudvijasahaḥ kṣāntas tasya gobhiḥ samā gatiḥ
english: He who from birth speaks truth, his senses restrained, forbearing toward elders and the twice-born and patient — his attainment is equal to that won by the gift of cattle.

sanskrit: na jātu brāhmaṇo vācyo yad avācyaṃ śacīpate manasā goṣu na druhyed govṛttir gonukampakaḥ
english: Never should a Brāhmaṇa be addressed with what ought not be spoken, O husband of Śacī; one should not even in mind do harm to cattle, but live by their ways and be compassionate to them.

sanskrit: satye dharme ca niratas tasya śakra phalaṃ śṛṇu gosahasreṇa samitā tasya dhenur bhavaty uta
english: For one devoted to truth and dharma — hear, O Śakra, his reward: his single cow becomes equal to a thousand.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya guṇair ebhir anvitasya phalaṃ śṛṇu tasyāpi śatatulyā gaur bhavatīti viniścayaḥ
english: Hear the reward of a Kṣatriya endowed with these same qualities: for him too one cow becomes equal to a hundred — such is the firm conclusion.

sanskrit: vaiśyasyaite yadi guṇās tasya pañcāśataṃ bhavet śūdrasyāpi vinītasya caturbhāgaphalaṃ smṛtam
english: If these qualities belong to a Vaiśya, for him it becomes equal to fifty; and for a disciplined Śūdra too the reward is reckoned as a quarter of that.

sanskrit: etac caivaṃ yo 'nutiṣṭheta yuktaḥ; satyena yukto guruśuśrūṣayā ca dāntaḥ kṣānto devatārcī praśāntaḥ; śucir buddho dharmaśīlo 'nahaṃvāk
english: And he who carries this out, ever devoted — joined to truth and to service of his elders, self-controlled, forbearing, a worshipper of the gods, serene, pure, awakened, of righteous disposition, free of self-assertion in speech —

sanskrit: mahat phalaṃ prāpnute sa dvijāya; dattvā dogdhrīṃ vidhinānena dhenum nityaṃ dadyād ekabhaktaḥ sadā ca; satye sthito guruśuśrūṣitā ca
english: that man attains a great reward by giving to a twice-born, according to this rule, a milch cow yielding milk. Let him give ever, taking but one meal a day, established in truth and a servant of his elders.

sanskrit: vedādhyāyī goṣu yo bhaktimāṃś ca; nityaṃ dṛṣṭvā yo 'bhinandeta gāś ca ā jātito yaś ca gavāṃ nameta; idaṃ phalaṃ śakra nibodha tasya
english: He who recites the Veda and is devoted to cattle, who ever rejoices at the sight of cows, and who bows to cattle from his very birth — mark, O Śakra, the reward that is his.

sanskrit: yat syād iṣṭvā rājasūye phalaṃ tu; yat syād iṣṭvā bahunā kāñcanena etat tulyaṃ phalam asyāhur agryaṃ; sarve santas tv ṛṣayo ye ca siddhāḥ
english: Whatever reward there is from performing the Rājasūya, whatever from sacrificing with abundant gold — equal and foremost to this, they declare his reward to be, all the holy ones and the seers and the perfected.

sanskrit: yo 'graṃ bhaktān kiṃ cid aprāśya dadyād; gobhyo nityaṃ govratī satyavādī śānto buddho gosahasrasya puṇyaṃ; saṃvatsareṇāpnuyāt puṇyaśīlaḥ
english: He who, without first tasting any morsel of his food, always offers the first portion to cattle — vowed to the cow, truth-speaking, serene, awakened — that man of meritorious character attains within a year the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: ya ekaṃ bhaktam aśnīyād dadyād ekaṃ gavāṃ ca yat daśa varṣāṇy anantāni govratī gonukampakaḥ
english: He who eats but one meal a day and gives even one share to cattle — vowed to the cow and compassionate to it — gains ten endless years of merit.

sanskrit: ekenaiva ca bhaktena yaḥ krītvā gāṃ prayacchati yāvanti tasya proktāni divasāni śatakrato tāvac chatānāṃ sa gavāṃ phalam āpnoti śāśvatam
english: And he who, taking but a single meal a day, buys a cow and gives it away — for as many days as are reckoned to him, O performer of a hundred rites, so many hundreds of cows' eternal reward does he obtain.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya phalaṃ hīdaṃ kṣatriye 'bhihitaṃ śṛṇu pañcavārṣikam etat tu kṣatriyasya phalaṃ smṛtam tato 'rdhena tu vaiśyasya śūdro vaiśyārdhataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: This is the reward of the Brāhmaṇa; now hear what is declared for the Kṣatriya. The Kṣatriya's reward is reckoned at five years' worth; the Vaiśya's at half of that, and the Śūdra's at half the Vaiśya's.

sanskrit: yaś cātmavikrayaṃ kṛtvā gāḥ krītvā saṃprayacchati yāvatīḥ sparśayed gā vai tāvat tu phalam aśnute lomni lomni mahābhāga lokāś cāsyākṣayāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: And he who, having even sold himself, buys cattle and gives them away, enjoys reward for as many cows as he can touch; for each hair upon them, O greatly blessed one, his worlds are reckoned imperishable.

sanskrit: saṃgrāmeṣv arjayitvā tu yo vai gāḥ saṃprayacchati ātmavikrayatulyās tāḥ śāśvatā viddhi kauśika
english: But he who, having won cattle in battle, gives them away — know those gifts to be equal to selling oneself, and eternal, O Kauśika.

sanskrit: alābhe yo gavāṃ dadyāt tiladhenuṃ yatavrataḥ durgāt sa tārito dhenvā kṣīranadyāṃ pramodate
english: He who, when no cattle can be had, gives a cow made of sesame, his vows controlled, is carried by that cow across the hard passage and rejoices upon a river of milk.

sanskrit: na tv evāsāṃ dānamātraṃ praśastaṃ; pātraṃ kālo goviśeṣo vidhiś ca kālajñānaṃ vipra gavāntaraṃ hi; duḥkhaṃ jñātuṃ pāvakādityabhūtam
english: Yet the mere giving of them is not praised; the worthy recipient, the time, the particular kind of cow, and the rite all matter. Knowledge of the right time, O Brāhmaṇa, and the differences among cattle are hard to know, being of the very nature of fire and the sun.

sanskrit: svādhyāyāḍhyaṃ śuddhayoniṃ praśāntaṃ; vaitānasthaṃ pāpabhīruṃ kṛtajñam goṣu kṣāntaṃ nātitīkṣṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ; vṛttiglānaṃ tādṛśaṃ pātram āhuḥ
english: Rich in Vedic recitation, of pure birth, serene, settled in the sacrificial fires, fearful of sin, grateful, forbearing toward cattle, not over-harsh, a refuge for others, yet worn by want of livelihood — such a one they call a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: vṛttiglāne sīdati cātimātraṃ; kṛṣyarthaṃ vā homahetoḥ prasūtyām gurvarthaṃ vā bālasaṃvṛddhaye vā; dhenuṃ dadyād deśakāle viśiṣṭe
english: When a man is sorely worn by want and sinking utterly, whether for the sake of tillage, or for the oblation, at a birthing, for an elder's need, or for the raising of a child — let one give a cow at a fitting place and time.

sanskrit: antarjātāḥ sukrayajñānalabdhāḥ; prāṇakrītā nirjitāś caukajāś ca kṛcchrotsṛṣṭāḥ poṣaṇābhyāgatāś ca; dvārair etair goviśeṣāḥ praśastāḥ
english: Born within one's own herd, gained by a good purchase, bought at the cost of one's life, won in battle, born together as a single litter, released from peril, or come to one for their nurture — by these means the choicest cattle are approved.

sanskrit: balānvitāḥ śīlavayopapannāḥ; sarvāḥ praśaṃsanti sugandhavatyaḥ yathā hi gaṅgā saritāṃ variṣṭhā; tathārjunīnāṃ kapilā variṣṭhā
english: Strong, of good temper and fit age, sweet-smelling — all such are praised; for as the Gaṅgā is the best among rivers, so the tawny cow is the best among the white.

sanskrit: tisro rātrīs tv adbhir upoṣya bhūmau; tṛptā gāvas tarpitebhyaḥ pradeyāḥ vatsaiḥ puṣṭaiḥ kṣīrapaiḥ supracārās; tryahaṃ dattvā gorasair vartitavyam
english: Having fasted three nights upon water and lain upon the ground, well-satisfied cattle should be given to satisfied recipients — cows with well-fed, milk-drinking calves, good in pasture; and for three days after the gift one should live on their milk-products alone.

sanskrit: dattvā dhenuṃ suvratāṃ sādhuvatsāṃ; kalyāṇavṛttām apalāyinīṃ ca yāvanti lomāni bhavanti tasyās; tāvanti varṣāṇi vasaty amutra
english: Having given a cow of gentle disposition, with a fine calf, of auspicious habits and not given to straying, for as many hairs as are upon her, so many years does one dwell in the world beyond.

sanskrit: tathānaḍvāhaṃ brāhmaṇāyātha dhuryaṃ; dattvā yuvānaṃ balinaṃ vinītam halasya voḍhāram anantavīryaṃ; prāpnoti lokān daśadhenudasya
english: Likewise, having given to a Brāhmaṇa a draught-ox fit for the yoke — young, strong, well-broken, a bearer of the plough, of boundless vigor — one attains the worlds of a giver of ten milch cows.

sanskrit: kāntāre brāhmaṇān gāś ca yaḥ paritrāti kauśika kṣemeṇa ca vimucyeta tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu aśvamedhakratos tulyaṃ phalaṃ bhavati śāśvatam
english: He who in the wilderness rescues Brāhmaṇas and cattle, O Kauśika, and brings them safely free — hear the fruit of his merit: his reward becomes eternal and equal to that of the horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: mṛtyukāle sahasrākṣa yāṃ vṛttim anukāṅkṣate lokān bahuvidhān divyān yad vāsya hṛdi vartate
english: At the hour of death, O thousand-eyed one, whatever state of being he longs for, whatever manifold heavenly worlds, or whatever dwells within his heart —

sanskrit: tat sarvaṃ samavāpnoti karmaṇā tena mānavaḥ gobhiś ca samanujñātaḥ sarvatra sa mahīyate
english: all that the man attains by that deed, and, granted favor by the cattle, he is everywhere held in honor.

sanskrit: yas tv etenaiva vidhinā gāṃ vaneṣv anugacchati tṛṇagomayaparṇāśī niḥspṛho niyataḥ śuciḥ
english: And he who by this very rite follows the cattle into the forests, eating grass, cow-dung, and leaves, free of craving, restrained and pure —

sanskrit: akāmaṃ tena vastavyaṃ muditena śatakrato mama loke suraiḥ sārdhaṃ loke yatrāpi cecchati
english: that man, desireless and glad, O performer of a hundred rites, must dwell in my world together with the gods, in whatever world he may also wish.

sanskrit: indra uvāca jānan yo gām apahared vikrīyād vārthakāraṇāt etad vijñātum icchāmi kā nu tasya gatir bhavet
english: Indra said: He who knowingly carries off a cow, or sells it for the sake of gain — this I wish to understand: what indeed is his destiny?

sanskrit: brahmovāca bhakṣārthaṃ vikrayārthaṃ vā ye 'pahāraṃ hi kurvate dānārthaṃ vā brāhmaṇāya tatredaṃ śrūyatāṃ phalam
english: Brahmā said: As for those who carry off a cow — whether to eat it, to sell it, or to give it to a Brāhmaṇa — hear in this matter what the fruit shall be.

sanskrit: vikrayārthaṃ hi yo hiṃsyād bhakṣayed vā niraṅkuśaḥ ghātayānaṃ hi puruṣaṃ ye 'numanyeyur arthinaḥ
english: He who, unbridled, would slay a cow to sell it or to eat it, and those self-seeking men who would consent to the one who has it killed —

sanskrit: ghātakaḥ khādako vāpi tathā yaś cānumanyate yāvanti tasyā lomāni tāvad varṣāṇi majjati
english: the slayer, the eater, and likewise he who gives his consent — for as many hairs as are upon that cow, so many years does he sink in hell.

sanskrit: ye doṣā yādṛśāś caiva dvijayajñopaghātake vikraye cāpahāre ca te doṣā vai smṛtāḥ prabho
english: Whatever faults, and of whatever kind, attach to one who ruins a twice-born's sacrifice, those very faults are declared to attach to the selling and the carrying off of a cow, O lord.

sanskrit: apahṛtya tu yo gāṃ vai brāhmaṇāya prayacchati yāvad dāne phalaṃ tasyās tāvan nirayam ṛcchati
english: But he who carries off a cow and then gives it to a Brāhmaṇa — for as long as the reward of that gift would last, so long does he descend into hell.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇām āhur gopradāne mahādyute suvarṇaṃ paramaṃ hy uktaṃ dakṣiṇārtham asaṃśayam
english: Gold, they say, is the sacrificial fee in the gift of a cow, O greatly resplendent one; gold is declared the supreme thing for the purpose of the fee, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: gopradānaṃ tārayate sapta pūrvāṃs tathā parān suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā tāvad dviguṇam ucyate
english: The gift of a cow carries across seven ancestors and seven descendants; and when gold is given as the fee, the deliverance is said to be twofold.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ paramaṃ dānaṃ suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇā parā suvarṇaṃ pāvanaṃ śakra pāvanānāṃ paraṃ smṛtam
english: Gold is the supreme gift, gold is the highest fee; gold is purifying, O Śakra, and is reckoned the foremost among purifiers.

sanskrit: kulānāṃ pāvanaṃ prāhur jātarūpaṃ śatakrato eṣā me dakṣiṇā proktā samāsena mahādyute
english: Gold they declare to be the purifier of lineages, O performer of a hundred rites; thus has the matter of the fee been told by me in brief, O greatly resplendent one.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etat pitāmahenoktam indrāya bharatarṣabha indro daśarathāyāha rāmāyāha pitā tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: This was spoken by the Grandsire to Indra, O bull of the Bhāratas; Indra told it to Daśaratha, and the father then told it to Rāma.

sanskrit: rāghavo 'pi priyabhrātre lakṣmaṇāya yaśasvine ṛṣibhyo lakṣmaṇenoktam araṇye vasatā vibho
english: Rāghava in turn told it to his dear brother, the glorious Lakṣmaṇa; and by Lakṣmaṇa, dwelling in the forest, it was told to the seers, O lord.

sanskrit: pāraṃparyāgataṃ cedam ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ durdharaṃ dhārayām āsū rājānaś caiva dhārmikāḥ upādhyāyena gaditaṃ mama cedaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: And this, come down through the succession, the seers of strict vows held fast though it is hard to hold, and the righteous kings likewise; and this was told to me too by my teacher, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ brāhmaṇo nityaṃ vaded brāhmaṇasaṃsadi yajñeṣu gopradāneṣu dvayor api samāgame
english: The Brāhmaṇa who would ever recite this in an assembly of Brāhmaṇas, at sacrifices, at the giving of cattle, and at the meeting of the two —

sanskrit: tasya lokāḥ kilākṣayyā daivataiḥ saha nityadā iti brahmā sa bhagavān uvāca parameśvaraḥ
english: for him, they say, the worlds are imperishable forever, together with the gods — thus spoke the blessed Brahmā, the supreme lord.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca visrambhito 'haṃ bhavatā dharmān pravadatā vibho pravakṣyāmi tu saṃdehaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have been given confidence by you as you declare the dharmas, O lord; yet I shall set forth a doubt — resolve it for me, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: vratānāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ proktaṃ kīdṛśaṃ vā mahādyute niyamānāṃ phalaṃ kiṃ ca svadhītasya ca kiṃ phalam
english: What reward is declared for vows, and of what kind, O greatly resplendent one? What is the reward of restraints, and what the reward of diligent study?

sanskrit: damasyeha phalaṃ kiṃ ca vedānāṃ dhāraṇe ca kim adhyāpane phalaṃ kiṃ ca sarvam icchāmi veditum
english: What here is the reward of self-restraint, and what in the retention of the Vedas? What is the reward in teaching them? All this I wish to know.

sanskrit: apratigrāhake kiṃ ca phalaṃ loke pitāmaha tasya kiṃ ca phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ yaḥ saṃprayacchati
english: And what reward in the world is there for one who accepts no gifts, O Grandsire? And what reward, seen or heard of, for one who bestows them?

sanskrit: svakarmaniratānāṃ ca śūrāṇāṃ cāpi kiṃ phalam satye ca kiṃ phalaṃ proktaṃ brahmacarye ca kiṃ phalam
english: And what is the reward of those devoted to their own duty, and of the heroes as well? What reward is declared for truth, and what for chastity?

sanskrit: pitṛśuśrūṣaṇe kiṃ ca mātṛśuśrūṣaṇe tathā ācāryaguruśuśrūṣāsv anukrośānukampane
english: And what in the service of one's father, and likewise in the service of one's mother, in the service of preceptor and elder, in mercy and in compassion?

sanskrit: etat sarvam aśeṣeṇa pitāmaha yathātatham vettum icchāmi dharmajña paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: All this in full and exactly as it is, O Grandsire, I wish to know, O knower of dharma; for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yo vrataṃ vai yathoddiṣṭaṃ tathā saṃpratipadyate akhaṇḍaṃ samyag ārabdhaṃ tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: He who undertakes a vow exactly as it has been prescribed, unbroken and rightly begun — for him the worlds are everlasting.

sanskrit: niyamānāṃ phalaṃ rājan pratyakṣam iha dṛśyate niyamānāṃ kratūnāṃ ca tvayāvāptam idaṃ phalam
english: The reward of the restraints, O king, is seen plainly here in this world; and this reward of the restraints and of the sacrifices has been won by you.

sanskrit: svadhītasyāpi ca phalaṃ dṛśyate 'mutra ceha ca ihaloke 'rthavān nityaṃ brahmaloke ca modate
english: And the reward of diligent study too is seen both there and here; in this world he is ever possessed of substance, and in the world of Brahmā he rejoices.

sanskrit: damasya tu phalaṃ rājañ śṛṇu tvaṃ vistareṇa me dāntāḥ sarvatra sukhino dāntāḥ sarvatra nirvṛtāḥ
english: But hear from me at length, O king, the reward of self-restraint: the self-restrained are happy everywhere, the self-restrained are everywhere at peace.

sanskrit: yatrecchāgāmino dāntāḥ sarvaśatruniṣūdanāḥ prārthayanti ca yad dāntā labhante tan na saṃśayaḥ
english: The self-restrained go wherever they wish and are slayers of all foes; and whatever the self-restrained seek, that they obtain — there is no doubt of it.

sanskrit: yujyante sarvakāmair hi dāntāḥ sarvatra pāṇḍava svarge tathā pramodante tapasā vikrameṇa ca
english: For the self-restrained are united with all desired things everywhere, O Pāṇḍava, and they rejoice in heaven through their austerity and their valor.

sanskrit: dānair yajñaiś ca vividhair yathā dāntāḥ kṣamānvitāḥ dātā kupyati no dāntas tasmād dānāt paro damaḥ
english: Just as the self-restrained, endowed with forbearance, prosper by gifts and by sacrifices of many kinds — yet the giver may grow angry, the self-restrained never does; therefore self-restraint is higher than giving.

sanskrit: yas tu dadyād akupyan hi tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ krodho hanti hi yad dānaṃ tasmād dānāt paro damaḥ
english: But he who gives without growing angry — for him the worlds are everlasting; for anger destroys the gift, and therefore self-restraint is higher than giving.

sanskrit: adṛśyāni mahārāja sthānāny ayutaśo divi ṛṣīṇāṃ sarvalokeṣu yānīto yānti devatāḥ
english: There are unseen abodes by the tens of thousands in heaven, O great king — the abodes of the seers, to which the gods proceed throughout all the worlds.

sanskrit: damena yāni nṛpate gacchanti paramarṣayaḥ kāmayānā mahat sthānaṃ tasmād dānāt paro damaḥ
english: To these, O lord of men, the supreme seers proceed through self-restraint, longing for that great abode; therefore self-restraint is higher than giving.

sanskrit: adhyāpakaḥ parikleśād akṣayaṃ phalam aśnute vidhivat pāvakaṃ hutvā brahmaloke narādhipa
english: The teacher, through his toil, enjoys an imperishable reward, having duly offered oblation into the fire, in the world of Brahmā, O ruler of men.
